verdict.rationale: LobeHub Desktop ships a built-in terminal with multiple active sessions, and it can install and run MCP connectors on your machine. It can also connect local agents, including coding CLIs. Together these point to a local execution surface, but no evidence explicitly shows the assistant itself running shell commands or editing files. Execution appears to happen through MCP connectors or external coding agents. Missing for 10: explicit docs that the agent executes commands and edits local files, permission and approval controls for exec, file-edit tooling, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, the assistant can run commands and edit files on my machine — a real exec surface, not just chat about what to do

citations.quote: The desktop terminal now has clearer tabs, right-click actions to close one or all other sessions, smoother open and close transitions, and faster rendering for active terminals.
Desktop can now install and run MCP connectors that live on your machine or your local network.
create agents here or connect external agents, including coding CLIs and personal agent platforms.
